trigger: Reciprocal cross-field peer review exposed a Poisson-EM initialization/convergence overclaim, a unique-maximum example typo and an IFT converse overclaim.

sources.title: Shepp and Vardi, Maximum Likelihood Reconstruction for Emission Tomography
sources.journal: IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging MI-1(2),113–122
sources.scopeRead: All10scanned pages, including Sections I–IV, Appendix I convergence/KKT proof, Appendix II code and references. Serial OCR used OMP_THREAD_LIMIT=1; full OCR text read, not just the abstract.

anchors.claim: Nonnegative detector-response probabilities and detection-efficiency normalization; use detected intensity lambdaPrime_j=s_j*x_j and p_ij=a_ij/s_j for a general finite nonnegative response matrix.
Concave Poisson likelihood, strictly positive initial estimate, EM multiplicative update, zero/zero defined as zero, likelihood improvement and total detected-count identity.

Boundary KKT conditions and convergence argument explicitly depend on a positive start; monotonicity alone is not the full image-convergence argument. The maximum need not be unique and the returned estimator can depend on initialization.

sources.title: Hudson and Larkin, Accelerated Image Reconstruction using Ordered Subsets of Projection Data
sources.journal: Published version IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging13(4),601–609
sources.version: Complete nine-page primary manuscript, placeholder IEEE VOL.XX/NO.Y/MONTH1994, internal pages100–108; submittedJanuary1993/revisedOctober1993. Not the publisher pagination601–609. Published public OCR corroborates the title/authors/year and relevant formulations but is not substituted for a complete publisher PDF.
sources.access: Followed the explicit data-src PDF URL in the openly available Studylib viewer HTML. Unencrypted PDF, all9pages and figures1–9 present. No login, paywall workaround or access-control bypass. The separate /download link returned HTML and was not used.
sources.scopeRead: All nine pages: Sections I–VI, Figures1–9/captions, references and complete Appendix assumptions, count-preservation lemma, Propositions1–2/corollary and proofs. Text read in full; equation2 and both appendix pages visually inspected at full page size, Figures2–9 visually inspected and allpages inspected in contact sheet.

anchors.claim: Positive start; same response matrix forward projection and transpose numerator; exact subset-specific column-sum divisor; zero divisor leaves pixel unchanged; one subset recovers standardEM; full iteration means one pass over allsubsets.

Exact-data convergence discussion requires feasibility; noisy inconsistent data invalidate Appendix assumptions and may produce distinct limit points. Strong subset balance rate argument and special orthogonality monotonicity argument are conditional, not universal guarantees.

Simulation-specific acceleration and same per-pass cost; noise artifact can turn image MSE upward; subset level affects terminal data fit, image error and noisy-data cycle behavior. §VI explicitly leaves general convergence open and describes non-ML limits/cycles. Optional full-count rescaling in simulations is not part of update2 and is not silently added to the panel.

Feasible exact nonnegative projections, nonnegative response with supported rows, strictly positive start, normalized equal subset sensitivities, finite exhaustive subset stock and nearly-cyclic control support the stated feasible-solution convergence. The proof is not a noisy-data ML convergence theorem.

secondaryPublicPreview.scope: Public HTML OCR includes published601–609, same equations/sections, references and appendix. Complete primary manuscript, rather than assumptions about preview rendering or hidden assets, supplies closure.

sourceDisposition.osemPrimaryManuscript: complete and read; relevant equations/assumptions/figures verified

repairs.claim: Require nonnegative finite response and positive sensitivity on retained columns, support for positive counts, and a strictly positive start. State zero-bin convention, objective monotonicity/global optimum and conditional unique-image convergence separately; explain zero locking and nonidentifiability.

repairs.computation: Use exact same sparse weights in Ax, transpose backprojection and A^T1. Remove1e-9 denominator/likelihood floor and1e-12 sensitivity cutoff. Zero-count rays contribute0even at zero prediction; log likelihood is -Infinity for an unsupported positive count; update rejects such an invalid support rather than inventing a positive mean.

repairs.presentation: Add the already-supported S=1 option; label curve shortfall relative to best displayed iterate, not a certified ML optimum. Remove unconditional S-fold acceleration and always-improving image-error/likelihood claims for subsets. Disclose geometric ray-length response and large-mean normal sampling approximation.

repairs.claim: Unique-maximum example now has one candidate drawing K and all others lower, rather than m-1 sharing the maximum. No computation or source flag changed.
Singular A/B removes the IFT guarantee of smooth local output/inverse determination. It does not prove nonuniqueness of nonlinear solutions. No computation or source flag changed.

independentChecks.name: Actual sparse projector/transpose adjoint
independentChecks.claim: Recover A^Tz from the production EM update and sensitivity; independently compare components and dot(z,Ax)=dot(A^Tz,x).

independentChecks.name: Sensitivity-weighted count conservation at ordinary and1e-18response scales
independentChecks.claim: One full-data update yields sum_j s_j*x_j=sum_i y_i, including an empty zero-count ray; old numeric floors fail the tiny-scale case.

independentChecks.name: Zero bins, empty rays, unobserved columns and unsupported positive counts
independentChecks.claim: 0ln0 contributes0; y>0at zero mean is -Infinity; update rejects incompatible support; unobserved columns are inert.

independentChecks.name: Exact tiny-mean likelihood
independentChecks.claim: No positive floor is substituted into the Poisson objective.

independentChecks.name: Zero-locking counterexample and independent KKT optimum
independentChecks.claim: For A=[[1,1],[1,2]],y=[1,4],x0=[1,0], the update sticks at[2.5,0] below the global optimum[0,5/3]. At the latter point gradient=[-0.2,0], satisfying concave maximization KKT; a positive start approaches it monotonically.

validation.inspection: All10full-page/cropped-contact screenshots inspected: legible light/dark stage labels, positive means/no nonfinite readouts, S=1overlapping MLEM likelihood/error traces, actual subset response and distinct selected states. The panel has no draggable handles; all mode choices were native pointer clicks and range states used native keyboard events.
validation.sourceClosureFollowup: Only bibliography and verify metadata changed after the passing native screenshots; mathematical statement, computation and controls remained frozen. Focused static check rerun; no new browser run required for metadata-only source closure.
